clinicalPearls: Caused by germline loss-of-function variants in SDHB on chromosome 1p36, inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern with incomplete, age-related penetrance.
Unlike SDHD, the SDHB locus is not imprinted, so disease can arise regardless of which parent transmits the variant.
Carries the highest metastatic potential of all the SDHx genes, with a substantial proportion of tumours developing metastatic disease.
Tumours are predominantly extra-adrenal sympathetic paragangliomas of the retroperitoneum and abdomen, such as at the organ of Zuckerkandl, and are often solitary at presentation.
A noradrenergic and dopaminergic secretory profile is common; raised methoxytyramine is a marker of more aggressive and potentially metastatic behaviour.
Carriers are at increased risk of SDH-deficient renal cell carcinoma and, less commonly, gastrointestinal stromal tumour and pituitary adenoma.
Ga-DOTATATE PET is the preferred functional imaging modality, and loss of SDHB immunostaining confirms the SDH-deficient phenotype.
reference.pathophysiology: SDHB encodes the iron–sulphur subunit of mitochondrial complex II. A germline inactivating variant combined with somatic loss of the remaining wild-type allele abolishes succinate dehydrogenase activity and destabilises the assembled complex, so SDHB protein is lost on immunohistochemistry. Accumulated succinate acts as an oncometabolite, inhibiting alpha-ketoglutarate–dependent prolyl hydroxylases, stabilising hypoxia-inducible factors and inducing a pseudohypoxic, pro-angiogenic and hypermethylator phenotype. SDHB-deficient cells appear particularly prone to acquiring an invasive, metastatic phenotype, which underlies the disproportionate malignancy risk of this subtype compared with the other SDHx genes. Tumours arise chiefly in sympathetic paraganglia, explaining the predominance of catecholamine-secreting extra-adrenal lesions rather than parasympathetic head and neck tumours.
additionalDifferentials: SDHD-related paraganglioma (PGL1), more often multifocal in the head and neck
Retroperitoneal soft tissue sarcoma or neuroblastoma in younger patients
Metastatic neuroendocrine tumour of unknown primary
additionalInvestigations: Plasma free metanephrines including methoxytyramine, the dopamine metabolite
Targeted SDHB germline testing and cascade screening of at-risk relatives
Whole-body MRI or CT given the frequently extra-adrenal and multifocal tumours
Ga-DOTATATE PET for staging and detection of metastatic deposits
Renal imaging surveillance for SDH-deficient renal cell carcinoma
A structured lifelong surveillance programme beginning in childhood
redFlags: Biochemical or imaging evidence of metastatic spread such as skeletal, nodal or hepatic deposits
Markedly raised methoxytyramine indicating a dopaminergic and potentially aggressive tumour
Catecholamine crisis with severe hypertension, arrhythmia or cardiomyopathy
A new paraganglioma detected on surveillance in a known carrier
reference.prognosis: SDHB-related tumours carry the least favourable prognosis among the SDHx syndromes because of their high metastatic potential; completely resected localised tumours can do well, but metastatic disease significantly shortens survival and responds only partially to current systemic therapies.
pitfalls: Assuming a normal adrenaline or metanephrine result excludes an active tumour when a dopamine-secreting lesion is present.
Limiting imaging to the abdomen and missing multifocal or metastatic disease elsewhere.
Deferring genetic testing in apparently sporadic, single extra-adrenal paragangliomas, many of which harbour germline SDHB variants.
Underestimating lifelong risk and discontinuing surveillance after apparently curative surgery.
